content.text: I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all four figure briefs, and built a full source ledger against the disclosure.

input.summary:
Full ledger built and traced. I checked all 16 claims (claims 1-10 apparatus, 11-16 method) limitation by limitation, all 25 entries of the numeral ledger (100-140 and 202-216), every numbered part as it appears in the detailed description and in each of the four figure briefs, the Field, Background, Summary, Brief Description of Drawings, Detailed Description and Abstract, and traced each technical assertion to an affirmative USER passage in input/disclosure.md (the conversation transcript is truncated mid-sentence and adds nothing beyond the disclosure; input/brief.md was used only for title, applicant/inventor, no-priority and no-government-support formalities).

Traced and supported: branch limit lower than the sum of connector ratings; per-channel contactor, connector current sensor, control-pilot interface and local connector identifier; upstream branch current sensor measuring total current; isolated local bus to the connector interfaces and contactors; the stored per-session charging authorization, requested current, minimum sustaining current and energy-deficit value; the allocation-interval computation (subtract measured non-charging branch load and configurable safety reserve, assign minimum sustaining current first, distribute the remainder by energy deficit); pilot delivery of the assigned limit and connector-sensor verification; reduced pilot command followed, after a verification interval with branch current still above the limit, by opening contactors one at a time in a stored shedding order until branch current is below the limit (claims 1/11 and dependent claims 2/12); the three reclosure conditions including the randomized recovery delay (claims 3/13); welded-contactor recording above a leakage threshold with inhibition of the other contactors on the branch and operation of the local fault indicator (claims 4/14); the isolated local bus (claim 5); network interface, signed local authorization token and last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory, outage behaviour and the token-authorized/unexpired gate on new sessions (claims 6/7/15); tamper-evident meter-record sequence and upload on return of communication (claim 8); and the service-input mapping by one low-energy pilot transition at a time with storage only after the responding sensor agrees (claims 9/10/16). Claim and specification terminology is identical throughout ("assigned current limit", "reduced pilot command", "verification interval", "stored shedding order", "leakage threshold", "randomized recovery delay", "signed local authorization token", "last accepted branch limit", "tamper-evident local sequence", "low-energy pilot transition"), each numeral denotes exactly one part in exactly one sense, the FIG. 4 column of eight shapes and its two return paths match the described flow (210 loop-back to 202, 216 loop-back to 202, 214 welded branch to a terminator), no section lines exist so no view designations are at issue, and no drafting note, placeholder, open question, unresolved alternative or internal comment remains. The Abstract is a single paragraph of about 146 words. Background prior-art characterizations were not traced to the disclosure, per instruction.

Two items are not fully supported or not internally complete and are reported: (1) FIG. 1 verbalizes the branch current sensor as interrupting the branch conductor, asserting a series break in the power path that the disclosure never states, while the same application depicts the connector current sensor with a neutral straddle convention; (2) FIG. 3's line to the local fault indicator has no specified origin, unlike every other line in that brief, leaving a free end inside the edge controller rectangle. Both have filing-clean automatic fixes confined to the figure briefs; no application text needs a speculative shape or optional embodiment added.

findings.title: FIG. 1 asserts the branch current sensor is inserted in series in the branch conductor, a connection the disclosure never states
findings.where: figures/FIG-1.md, branch current sensor paragraph and the numeral 104 entry
findings.detail: The disclosure affirmatively discloses the branch current sensor and its location and function, but says nothing about how it is joined to the conductor. The figure brief verbalizes a specific connection topology: the conductor terminates on the left side of the sensor block and restarts at its right side, so the branch conductor is broken at the sensor. That is a series-insertion assertion (a device carrying the full branch current in the power path) rather than a neutral depiction of a sensor located on the conductor, and it is the kind of connection/topology statement that conveys technical substance. It is also inconsistent with the convention the same application uses for the same class of part: FIG. 2 shows the connector current sensor as an outline that merely 'straddles' the run and is expressly 'shown schematically', whereas the FIG. 1 brief neither says 'shown schematically' for element 104 nor leaves the conductor continuous. The description text is neutral ('A branch current sensor 104 is arranged on the branch conductor 102 upstream of the contactors of the connector channels and measures a branch current'), so only the figure brief needs correcting.
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-1.md): "An empty rectangle stands on this horizontal line in its left portion and represents the branch current sensor. The horizontal line meets its left side and leaves its right side, so that the rectangle interrupts the line and its interior is blank and closed." and "104 branch current sensor: leader ends on the outline of the rectangle that interrupts the horizontal line." Nearest inventor passage (input/disclosure.md): "A branch current sensor measures total current upstream of the connector contactors." No affirmative USER passage anywhere in the disclosure or conversation states that the branch current sensor is connected in series in, or interrupts, the branch conductor; compare the contactor, for which the disclosure does affirmatively support interruption ("Each connector has a controllable contactor" that the controller "opens").
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-1.md, replace the branch current sensor paragraph with: "An empty rectangle stands on this horizontal line in its left portion and represents the branch current sensor, shown schematically. The horizontal line passes through the rectangle and continues on both sides of it, so that the rectangle straddles the line without interrupting it, and the interior of the rectangle is otherwise blank." And replace the numeral entry with: "104 branch current sensor: leader ends on the outline of the rectangle that straddles the horizontal line." Make no change to draft/08-detailed-description.md, which is already neutral.

findings.title: FIG. 3 line to the local fault indicator has no specified origin, leaving an unanchored free end inside the edge controller
findings.detail: Every other line in the FIG. 3 brief is anchored at both ends or is expressly described as ending free: the network interface line 'runs upward from the network interface rectangle and crosses the upper side', the service input line 'runs left from the service input rectangle and crosses the left side', and each of the two descending lines 'meets the lower side of the large rectangle at its upper end and ends free below the large rectangle'. The fault indicator line specifies only its right endpoint and states that it 'crosses' the right side of the large rectangle, which places its left endpoint somewhere unspecified inside the blank interior of the edge controller. As written the brief does not determine the left endpoint and would produce a line with a dangling free end inside the controller box. The intended relationship in the description is a coupling between the edge controller as a whole and the indicator, which is satisfied by starting the line at the boundary of the edge controller rectangle.
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-3.md): "A further empty rectangle stands outside the large rectangle, beyond its right side in the upper right region, and represents the local fault indicator. A solid line crosses the right side of the large rectangle and meets the left side of the local fault indicator rectangle." Supporting description text (draft/08-detailed-description.md): "A local fault indicator 116 at the installation is coupled to the edge controller 106 and is operated by the edge controller 106 to signal a condition that requires attention at the equipment itself."
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-3.md, replace the second sentence with: "A short solid line runs rightward from the right side of the large rectangle and meets the left side of the local fault indicator rectangle, both of its ends being on those two outlines." No other change is required; the numeral 116 entry and the description remain as written.
